2607.15736.title: Better Starts, Better Ends: Bootstrapped Iterative Self-Reasoning Distillation for Compressed Reasoning
2607.15736.paper_summary: Large reasoning models often solve problems through long chain-of-thought (CoT) traces, yet much of this computation is spent on redundant derivations, repeated self-verification, and detours that do not improve the final answer. Existing on-policy self-distillation methods reduce this cost by matching a student model to a concise copy of itself on prefixes sampled from the student's own rollouts. We show that this objective has an initialization bottleneck. Since supervision is applied only to visited prefixes, training from a verbose base model places the KL loss on contexts that are often noisy, redundant, or already off track. In such regions, a concise teacher can provide only local corrections, while the student continues to explore trajectories that an efficient reasoner should avoid. In this paper, we propose BIRD(Bootstrapped Iterative Self-Reasoning Distillation), a two-stage self-reasoning distillation method that improves the rollout distribution before on-policy training. BIRD first samples concise solutions from the base model under a brevity instruction, keeps only answer-correct traces, and performs a lightweight prompt-switch SFT step. The traces are generated with the brevity instruction but learned under the original task prompt, turning instruction-induced conciseness into a default reasoning behavior. Starting from this warm model, BIRD then applies on-policy reverse-KL distillation with a concise self-teacher, now on cleaner and more informative prefixes. Across Qwen3 series models, BIRD achieves a stronger accuracy-efficiency trade-off than prompting and cold-start on-policy distillation on MATH-500 and AIME benchmarks. On Qwen3-8B, it improves MATH-500 accuracy from 86.2% to 92.0% while reducing the average response length from 3,099 to 1,115 tokens. These results highlight prefix support as a central factor in efficient reasoning distillation.
2607.15736.paper_summary_zh: 大型推理模型通常通過長鏈思考（CoT）痕跡來解決問題，但這些計算中有很多時間花費在冗餘的推導、重複的自我驗證和不改善最終答案的繞道上。現有的政策內自蒸餾方法通過將學生模型與其自身在學生自己展開的前綴上進行的簡潔複製進行匹配來減少這一成本。我們表明這一目標存在初始化瓶頸。由於監督僅應用於訪問的前綴，從冗長的基礎模型進行訓練會將KL損失放置在經常嘈雜、冗餘或已經偏離的上下文中。在這些區域，簡潔的教師只能提供局部修正，而學生則繼續探索一個高效推理者應該避免的軌跡。在本文中，我們提出了BIRD（引導式迭代自我推理蒸餾），這是一種兩階段的自我推理蒸餾方法，在政策內訓練之前改善展開分佈。BIRD首先在簡潔指令下從基礎模型中抽樣簡潔解決方案，僅保留答案正確的痕跡，並執行輕量級的提示切換SFT步驟。這些痕跡是在簡潔指令下生成的，但在原始任務提示下學習，將指令引起的簡潔性轉變為默認的推理行為。從這個預熱模型開始，BIRD然後在更乾淨和更具信息性的前綴上應用政策內的反KL蒸餾，使用簡潔的自我教師。在Qwen3系列模型中，BIRD在MATH-500和AIME基準上實現了比提示和冷啟動政策內蒸餾更強的準確性-效率權衡。在Qwen3-8B上，它將MATH-500的準確性從86.2%提高到92.0%，同時將平均響應長度從3,099減少到1,115個標記。這些結果突顯了前綴支持作為高效推理蒸餾中的一個核心因素。
